title: Amazing Fantasy
description: The anthology series created in the early 1960s that introduced Spider-Man in issue #15 (1962), written by Stan Lee and drawn by Steve Ditko. Cover of AF #15 by Jack Kirby.

title: The Amazing Spider-Man
description: The original Amazing Spider-Man ongoing series running from 1963 to 1998 across 441 issues, spanning Stan Lee through Tom DeFalco.

title: The Amazing Spider-Man (Vol. 2)
description: The relaunched Amazing Spider-Man volume covering the Howard Mackie, JMS, and Dan Slott eras through issue #700.

title: The Amazing Spider-Man (Vol. 3)
description: A short volume bridging the Superior Spider-Man era back to Peter Parker, written by Dan Slott.

title: The Amazing Spider-Man (Vol. 4)
description: Dan Slott's final Amazing Spider-Man volume, culminating in the landmark #800 and Go Down Swinging.

title: The Amazing Spider-Man (Vol. 5)
description: Nick Spencer's run restoring Peter Parker's classic status quo, featuring Sins Rising, Last Remains, and Beyond. (Head canon is that is the end of the whole Spider-Man series, we don't talk about anything past the Nick Spencer Run.)

title: Peter Parker, the Spectacular Spider-Man
description: The long-running companion to Amazing Spider-Man featuring Kraven's Last Hunt and many classic supporting stories. Acts as a sort of connective tissue to the ongoing Amazing Spider-Man series.

title: Spectacular Spider-Man
description: A short-lived revival of the Peter Parker, the Spectacular Spider-Man title, no retitled as Spectacular Spider-Man. Was released in the early 2000s.

title: Web of Spider-Man
description: Another companion Spider-Man series running from 1985 to 1995, featuring many crossover tie-in issues.

title: Spider-Man
description: Todd McFarlane's self-titled Spider-Man series, with all of it's 90s glory. Eventually the title was continued with other creative teams.

title: Superior Spider-Man
description: Dan Slott's bold status quo shift with Otto Octavius as the Superior Spider-Man, replacing Peter Parker for tight experimental 33 issue run.

title: Marvel Team-Up
description: A Spider-Man teams up with a different Marvel hero each issue across this long-running anthology series.

title: Spider-Man vs. Wolverine
description: A single issue one shot comic pitting Spider-Man against Wolverine in a Cold War thriller.

title: Spider-Man 2099
description: Set in the dystopian city of Nueva York in the year 2099, the series follows Miguel O'Hara as the new Spider-Man. Read this in all of its 90s glory.

title: Spider-Man: Blue
description: Jeph Loeb and Tim Sale's love letter to the early days of Spider-Man, focusing on Peter Parker's relationship with Gwen Stacy. A beautifully illustrated and emotionally resonant mini-series that captures the essence of Spider-Man

title: Ultimate Spider-Man (2000)
description: Brian Michael Bendis' iconic Ultimate Spider-Man series that reimagines Peter Parker's origin for the 21st century. A landmark run that helped launch the Ultimate Universe and redefines the character for a new generation.

title: Ultimate Spider-Man (2024)
description: Jonathan Hickman's revival of Ultimate Spider-Man, which is set in an entirely new Ultimate Universe. We follow an older Peter Parker who is a both a husband to Mary Jane Watson and a father to their children Richard and May. A bold new take on the character that explores the challenges of balancing family life with his newly acquired superhero responsibilities.

title: Invincible
description: Robert Kirkman's superhero epic following Mark Grayson, son of the world's greatest hero.

title: Hellboy
description: Mike Mignola's iconic Dark Horse series following Hellboy, a demon raised by the BPRD to fight supernatural threats.

title: Batman
description: The original Batman ongoing series running from 1940 to 2011, spanning the Golden Age through modern era (Before the New 52 relaunch).

title: Final Crisis (Batman issues)
description: Grant Morrison's DC event — Batman confronts Darkseid and is struck by the Omega Beams, apparently killed but actually sent back in time. Includes Batman #682-683.

title: Batman: Battle for the Cowl
description: Tony Daniel's 3-issue miniseries where the Bat-family fights over who becomes the new Batman after Bruce Wayne's death in Final Crisis. Dick Grayson ultimately takes the mantle.

title: The Return of Bruce Wayne
description: Grant Morrison's 6-issue miniseries following Bruce Wayne unstuck in time — traveling from prehistoric Gotham through Puritan, pirate, western, and noir eras before returning to the present.

title: Batman (New 52)
description: Scott Snyder and Greg Capullo's critically acclaimed New 52 Batman run, which follows a rebooted Batman and his Bat-Family as they face off against new and old threats in Gotham City.

title: Batman (Rebirth)
description: The DC Rebirth Batman series which serves as both a continuation of the New 52 and a relaunch, beginning with Tom King's run through James Tynion IV and Chip Zdarsky.

title: Detective Comics
description: Batman's home series since Detective Comics #27 (1939). The longest-running superhero comic in history.

title: Detective Comics (New 52)
description: The New 52 relaunch of Detective Comics running from 2011-2016 across 52 issues. Featured creative teams including Tony S. Daniel, John Layman, and Francis Manapul.

title: Batman: Legends of the Dark Knight
description: Anthology series featuring self-contained Batman stories set across different periods of his career.

title: Batman: Shadow of the Bat
description: An ongoing Batman series that played a key role in the Knightfall and No Man's Land crossovers.

title: Batman Eternal
description: Weekly Batman series that run concurrently to the New 52 Batman series. This limited series features a massive conspiracy threatening Gotham that involves the entire Bat-Family.

title: Batman: Year One
description: Frank Miller and David Mazzucchelli's definitive Batman origin story, originally published in Batman #404-407.

title: Batman: The Dark Knight Returns
description: Frank Miller and David Mazzucchelli's definitive Batman origin story, originally published in Batman #404-407.

title: Batman and Robin (2009)
description: Grant Morrison and Frank Quitely's series following Dick Grayson as Batman and Damian Wayne as Robin. Features Professor Pyg, the Red Hood, and the return of Doctor Hurt.

title: Batman Incorporated (Vol 1)
description: Grant Morrison's series where Bruce Wayne goes public as Batman's financier and establishes a global franchise of Batmen to fight the Leviathan organization led by Talia al Ghul.

title: Batman Incorporated (Vol 2)
description: Morrison's New 52 conclusion to his Batman saga — Talia al Ghul's Leviathan wages all-out war on Batman Incorporated, culminating in Damian Wayne's death.

title: Batman: The Killing Joke
description: Alan Moore and Brian Bolland's prestige one-shot. The Joker shoots and paralyzes Barbara Gordon, then tortures Commissioner Gordon to prove anyone can be driven insane by one bad day. The pivotal issue for Barbara's transition from Batgirl to Oracle.
